page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s3.large is a virtual instance based on the KVM hypervisor and built on the standard x86_64 processor architecture. Configured with 4 dedicated virtual CPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory, this instance presents a lean 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, yielding exactly 2.0 GB of RAM per processor core. This resource allocation aligns the system with compute-skewed processing environments where CPU throughput is prioritized over massive memory caches.

Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent on this instance, and it provides no built-in local disk storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Consequently, persistent storage and operating system images must be attached externally via network-attached cloud block storage volumes. System architectures utilizing ecs.s3.large need to factor in network block I/O performance when designing data-heavy operations.

From an infrastructure perspective, the dedicated allocation of its 4 vCPUs ensures predictable compute performance free from CPU credit exhaustion or noisy-neighbor resource throttling common to shared-core or burstable tiers. The tight memory allotment offers strong cost efficiency for CPU-dominant tasks, preventing expenditure on unutilized RAM capacity.

Given its hardware specifications, Alibaba Cloud ecs.s3.large is suitable for stateless batch processing, distributed build tasks, continuous integration pipelines, batch web application serving, and backend worker services where memory footprint remains modest.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s3.large is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory distribution of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains zero GPUs and provides no integrated local storage, requiring cloud block storage for file systems and data retention. By utilizing fully dedicated vCPUs rather than a shared or burstable CPU model, ecs.s3.large avoids execution throttling and provides consistent computational throughput. The compact memory footprint makes it cost-effective for CPU-centric tasks that do not demand extensive RAM pools. This profile makes it appropriate for distributed microservices, CI/CD runners, batch processing workers, and front-facing web servers with moderate memory demands.
